title: Fish Keychains
subject: Contracts
stem:
Daniel runs a private Jonah-themed escape-room booth for Christian conventions. He called Lydia, a wholesaler of ordinary catalog-stock olivewood fish keychains, and said that he would buy 800 keychains for his booth if Lydia could get them to him within seven days. Daniel did not mention a price. At the time of the call, the market price for 800 of those keychains was about $9,600.

Lydia did not say yes or no on the call. Six days later, her driver arrived at Daniel’s storage unit with the 800 keychains and an invoice for $9,600. Before the driver arrived, the convention organizer had canceled Daniel’s booth space. Daniel refused to receive the keychains or pay the invoice.

Is there an enforceable contract between Daniel and Lydia?
call: Is there an enforceable contract between Daniel and Lydia?

choices.A: Yes, because Lydia relied on an implied promise to pay when she brought the keychains to Daniel.
choices.B: No, because the parties never agreed on the price of the keychains.
choices.C: Yes, because leaving the price open does not prevent a valid sale-of-goods contract when the parties otherwise intended to contract.
choices.D: No, because the parties did not put their agreement in writing.

rightExplanation: D is correct. This is a sale of ordinary goods for about $9,600, and no writing exists. Gold Key: a sale-of-goods deal priced at $500 or more must satisfy the UCC writing requirement unless an exception applies. Lydia’s delivery did not solve that problem because Daniel refused to receive and accept the keychains. Silver Key: lock the call word enforceable before rewarding a Yes answer; formation and enforceability are separate gates.

c3.label: Frame
c3.text: The call asks enforceability, not merely whether a contract could form.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: A points to Lydia’s delivery/reliance. That is not the dispositive gate. Daniel refused the goods. Filter broken: NOT_RESPONSIVE.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: B says no contract because no price. Gold Key defeats it: open price can be filled under the UCC. Filter broken: NOT_TRUE.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: C states the open-price rule. It is attractive and true as far as formation goes, but it misses the writing gate. Filter broken: NOT_RESPONSIVE.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text: D. No writing, sale of goods over $500, no acceptance/payment exception.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: The anchor decides the item: UCC writing gate before open-price formation.

studentScript: Call is enforceable. Goods are over $500, no writing, and the buyer refused the goods. Open price does not save enforceability. Pick D.

A.signal: The choice talks about seller reliance, but the call asks enforceability against a buyer who refused the goods.
A.lawyer: UCC § 2-201(3)(c) requires goods received and accepted, or payment made and accepted, for this partial-performance path.

B.signal: Gold Key: missing price alone does not defeat a sale-of-goods contract.
B.lawyer: UCC § 2-305 permits a contract for sale even though the price is not settled if the parties intended a contract.

C.signal: Silver Key: the choice answers formation, not the enforceability writing gate.
C.lawyer: UCC § 2-305 does not override UCC § 2-201's writing requirement for goods priced at $500 or more.

D.signal: The choice matches the enforceability call and the writing-gate fact.
D.lawyer: UCC § 2-201 makes the unwritten sale-of-goods agreement unenforceable absent an exception.

goldKeys.statement: For goods priced at $500 or more, the UCC writing gate must be satisfied before the oral deal can be enforced. Mere shipment does not unlock the partial-performance exception when the buyer refuses to receive and accept the goods.
goldKeys.trigger: Oral sale of goods worth thousands, no writing, delivery refused.
goldKeys.unlocks: The no-writing answer and the delivery/reliance trap.

goldKeys.statement: Open price and writing are separate gates. UCC § 2-305 can fill a missing price term, but it does not satisfy the UCC § 2-201 writing requirement.
goldKeys.trigger: A Yes answer says the missing price term does not defeat the deal.

silverKeys.statement: Lock the call word enforceable before grading the Yes choices. A choice can prove formation with an open price and still miss the separate writing gate.
silverKeys.trigger: The call asks enforceable contract, while a choice talks only about price-term formation.

remediation.title: Formation is not enforceability
remediation.signal: Oral goods deal over $500 with no writing and a missing price term.
remediation.studentMove: Check the writing gate before rewarding the open-price rule.
remediation.tinyRule: Open price can be filled, but the UCC writing gate still blocks enforcement unless an exception applies.
remediation.trap: Yes because open price does not defeat contract formation.
